recommended_next_phase: If the hybrid remote-WebAuthn direction is the one the human wants pursued, the narrowest next phase is a remote-WebAuthn contract/architecture freeze: resolve the RP-ID/origin question explicitly, define the new provider_profile value and evidence schema, define challenge-binding contract fields -- still no implementation, no hardware, no makeCredential. summary: Read-only inspection and architecture-analysis phase, revised mid-phase from a Dell-local-attachment assumption to a Mac-attached-authenticator + multi-authenticator/remote-WebAuthn investigation, at the human's explicit direction. Preserved the already-obtained hac-dell zero-device result (lsusb/CtapHidDevice.list_devices()/discover_fido2() all zero, no hardware mutation) without repeating that work. Re-verified hac-dell host identity, deployed revision cdb77b75fc8bbca04340c7f25c405db3b07d32f7 (unchanged, clean), HMIC v1.7/38 re-derivation (validator VALID, matching 2N.5's own activation byte-for-byte), venv (fido2==1.2.0, cryptography==44.0.3), and Protected Root/Trust-Enrollment absence, all fresh. Read-only inspected the Mac-attached authenticator via ioreg (direct USB-C attach, no hub; idVendor=0x1050/Yubico, idProduct=0x0402) and python-fido2's non-mutating authenticatorGetInfo (versions FIDO_2_1/U2F_V2, transports=['nfc','usb'], aaguid=b7d3f68e88a6471e9ecf2df26d041ede, rk=True, clientPin=True, ES256 supported). Cross-referenced the AAGUID against an independently fetched community Yubico AAGUID table (external research, distinguished from repository evidence) to identify Security Key C NFC by Yubico, firmware 5.7.4, FIDO2 L2 -- FIDO-only product line, ES256-compatible with PCAE's current enrollment allowlist. Externally researched and tabulated YubiKey 5C/5C NFC for comparison. Read hatp_hardware_credentials.py/hatp_bootstrap.py fresh, confirmed via 9 new disposable tests against the real parsers that the registry already supports multiple simultaneous HardwareCredentialRecords and multiple SignerRecords sharing one principal_id -- no schema change needed for registered-credential multiplicity; DeploymentBinding remains the single explicit-selection point (exactly one per repository_id, confirmed via duplicate-rejection test). The one singleton assumption found is at the physical hardware layer (devices[0] in enroll_credential()/request_signature()), unchanged from prior findings. Investigated a remote-WebAuthn architecture (analysis only): enrollment evidence maps onto the existing schema without a schema change; remote signing cannot reuse the fixed internal hatp.pcae.local RP-ID/origin unmodified -- a real HTTPS origin is required for a browser WebAuthn ceremony, flagged as the key open design question. Recommended a hybrid architecture (existing local/raw FIDO2 provider retained + new remote-WebAuthn provider, sharing governance) -- nothing implemented. No production source changed. No makeCredential anywhere, on either host.

test_results.remote_webauthn_rp_id_finding: Phase 149O.20L.7O.2N.6: Fresh source read of hatp_fido2_provider.py's request_signature()/verify(): both use fixed internal constants _HATP_RP_ID='hatp.pcae.local' and _HATP_ORIGIN='pcae-hatp://hatp.pcae.local', explicitly documented as 'HATP is not a web origin'.
